propositions.text: The principal and associate appellants, Pakistani citizens, appealed the RPD decision rejecting their refugee claims.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX(Principal Appellant) and XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX(Associate Appellant(s)), citizens of Pakistan, appealed a decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD), dated March 19, 2018, rejecting their claims for refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: The court states that the principal and associate appellants, Pakistani citizens, appealed the RPD decision rejecting their refugee claims.

propositions.text: The RAD dismisses the appeal and confirms the RPD decision that appellants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection under IRPA section 111(1)(a).
propositions.quote: The Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) dismisses the appeal and confirms the decision of the RPD that the Appellants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection, pursuant to section 111(1)(a) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal and confirms the RPD decision that appellants are not Convention refugees or persons in need of protection under IRPA.

propositions.text: The principal appellant's BOC was adopted by all appellants, alleging extortion by a political party-affiliated organized crime group starting 2011.
propositions.quote: The Basis of Claim (BOC) narrative of the principal Appellant was adopted by all of the Appellants. They alleged in the BOC that the principal Appellant owned a XXXX XXXX in Karachi, and that beginning in XXXX 2011 he was subjected to extortion demands from XXXX XXXX, an organized crime group affiliated with the political party XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX.

propositions.text: In 2013, the group demanded monthly payments and the principal appellant agreed to pay a specified amount monthly.
propositions.quote: They alleged that in XXXX 2013 members of XXXX XXXX began to demand monthly payments and the principal Appellant was forced to agree to pay ?XXXX XXXX XXXX monthly.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the principal appellant's BOC alleges extortion by a political party-affiliated group from 2011 and monthly payments from 2013.

propositions.text: The principal appellant's son was kidnapped in 2014 and released after ransom payment; in 2015, the appellant had to pay a sum and moved family to Lahore for safety.
propositions.quote: The son of the principal Appellant (the associate Appellant) was kidnapped in XXXX 2014 and released upon payment of XXXX lakhs in a ransom. In XXXX 2015 the principal Appellant was required to pay XXXX XXXX XXXX and was granted XXXX days to acquire this money. Before the end of that period he closed his XXXX and the family moved to Lahore for safety in XXXX 2015.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the principal appellant's son was kidnapped in 2014 and the family moved to Lahore in 2015 for safety after ransom and payment demands.

propositions.text: In Lahore, the principal appellant paid police bribes twice; family returned to Karachi in 2015, did not resume school or work, and decided to leave the country.
propositions.quote: While in Lahore, the principal Appellant was required to pay bribes to the police on two occasions. The Appellants returned to Karachi in XXXX 2015 and resided with the principal Appellant's in-laws. The family did not resume school or employment and decided to leave the country. The whole family eventually arrived in Canada and made a refugee claim.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the family paid police bribes in Lahore, returned to Karachi, did not resume normal life, and then fled to Canada.

propositions.text: Neighbours advised appellants that strangers asked about the principal appellant; nephew was accosted by men seeking him.
propositions.quote: The Appellants have been advised by their neighbours in Karachi that strangers have asked about the principal Appellant two or three times. They alleged that their nephew was accosted by men looking for the principal Appellant, when he went to check on their home.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found neighbours reported strangers asking about the principal appellant and nephew was accosted by men seeking him.

propositions.text: The RPD heard the claim on February 28, 2018, and rejected it on March 19, 2018, finding a viable internal flight alternative in Islamabad.
propositions.quote: The claim for refugee protection was heard by the RPD on February 28, 2018. In a written decision dated March 19, 2018 the RPD rejected the claim finding that the Appellants have a viable internal flight alternative (IFA) in Islamabad.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker heard the claim in February 2018 and rejected it in March 2018, finding a viable internal flight alternative in Islamabad.

propositions.text: The appellants argue they were misrepresented by former counsel and filed a complaint with the Law Society of Alberta.
propositions.quote: The Appellants argue that they were misrepresented by their former counsel and have filed a formal complaint against her with the Law Society of Alberta.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue they were misrepresented by former counsel and filed a complaint with the Law Society of Alberta.

propositions.text: The appellants argue the RPD erred by not applying Chairperson's Guidelines on Child Refugee Claimants and not assessing Convention on the Rights of the Child impact.
propositions.quote: The Appellants argue that the RPD erred in failing to apply the Chairperson's Guidelines on Child Refugee Claimants1 and by not determining the impact of the Convention on the Rights of the Child on the minor Appellants' claims;

propositions.text: The appellants argue the RPD's assessment of personal evidence was unreasonable, incorrect, and breached procedural fairness.
propositions.quote: the RPD's assessment of their personal evidence was unreasonable, incorrect and in breach of procedural fairness;

propositions.text: The appellants allege breach of natural justice due to incompetence of former counsel.
propositions.quote: that there was a breach of natural justice due to the incompetence of their former counsel;

propositions.text: The appellants argue the RPD failed to assess and consider evidence and provide a forward-looking risk assessment.
propositions.quote: and that the RPD failed to assess and consider the evidence and provide a forward-looking assessment of risk.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants argue the RPD erred on child claimant guidelines, evidence assessment, natural justice breach, and risk assessment failures.

propositions.text: RAD must proceed without hearing on RPD record but may accept documentary evidence and submissions from Minister and appellant.
propositions.quote: As provided for in subsection 110(3) of the IRPA, with certain exceptions, the RAD must proceed without a hearing on the basis of the record of the proceedings of the RPD, and may accept documentary evidence and written submissions from the Minister and the person who is the subject of the appeal.

propositions.text: Appellant may present only evidence arising after rejection or not reasonably available or not reasonably expected to be presented at rejection time.
propositions.quote: Subsection 110(4) of the IRPA provides that the person who is the subject of the appeal may present only evidence that arose after the rejection of their claim, or that was not reasonably available, or that the person could not reasonably have been expected in the circumstances to have presented, at the time of the rejection.

paragraphs.summary: The court states RAD must proceed without hearing on RPD record but may accept new evidence only if it arose after rejection or was not reasonably available then.

propositions.text: Appellants request letters from two friends be entered as evidence, which postdate claim rejection and address relevant issues.
propositions.quote: The Appellants request that letters from a friend, XXXX XXXX XXXX, the principal Appellant's sister-in-law, and a letter from another friend, XXXX XXXX, be entered into evidence.

propositions.text: RAD accepts these letters as they postdate claim rejection and address relevant issues; weight to be assessed later.
propositions.quote: The RAD will accept these letters as they postdate the rejection of the claim and address the issues relevant to the claim. The RAD will assess the weight to be assigned to these letters in its analysis of the appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants request letters from friends be admitted; the court accepts them as postdating rejection and relevant, to assess weight later.

propositions.text: Appellants request a letter from a Karachi lawyer be entered into evidence, postdating claim rejection and dealing with relevant issues.
propositions.quote: The Appellants request that a letter 3from a lawyer based in Karachi be entered into evidence.

propositions.text: RAD accepts the lawyer's letter as it postdates claim rejection and deals with relevant issues; weight to be assessed later.
propositions.quote: The RAD will accept this letter as it postdates the rejection of the claim and deals with relevant issues. The RAD will assess the weight to be put to this letter in its analysis of the appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants request a Karachi lawyer's letter be admitted; the court accepts it as postdating rejection and relevant, to assess weight later.

propositions.text: Appellants submit newspaper articles and a recent FIR attached to lawyer's letter for evidence.
propositions.quote: Attached to the letter from the lawyer are newspaper articles and a recent First Information Report (FIR).

propositions.text: RAD accepts some 2018 newspaper articles but rejects other news items predating claim rejection and the FIR predating rejection.
propositions.quote: The RAD will only accept some of these items into evidence. These items are the article from the Weekly JANG dated XXXX XXXX, 2018; the article from the National dated XXXX XXXX, 2018; and the article from Dawn, dated XXXX XXXX, 2018. All of the other news items submitted predate the rejection of the claim and deal with issues that were already before the RPD. It is reasonable to expect in these circumstances that these items would have been submitted prior to the rejection of the claim. The RAD will not accept the FIR4 into evidence as it predates the rejection of the claim and would reasonably have been available through the same source that provided it in June 2018.

propositions.text: Two newspaper articles without publication names are rejected as their probative value cannot be assessed.
propositions.quote: Two of the newspaper articles do not reveal the name of the publication and so will not be accepted into evidence as it is not possible to assess the probative value of the items without knowing where they appeared.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants submit articles and an FIR; the court accepts some 2018 articles but rejects older items, the FIR, and unnamed publication articles.

propositions.text: Appellants provide photos and a 2017 newspaper article about a protest in Canada against Pakistan.
propositions.quote: The Appellants have additionally provided photographs of the principal Appellant attending a demonstration in Canada against Pakistan in 2017. They have provided a newspaper article from 2017 referring to this protest.

propositions.text: RAD rejects these documents as they predate claim rejection and were reasonably available at hearing time.
propositions.quote: The RAD will not accept these documents into evidence given that they predate the rejection of the claim and would have been reasonably available to the Appellants at the time of their hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants provide photos and a 2017 article about a protest; the court rejects them as predating claim rejection and reasonably available then.

propositions.text: Appellants request a 2012 IRB Response to Information Request on Mohajirs be entered into evidence.
propositions.quote: The Appellants ask that a Response to Information Request from 20127 dealing with the situation and treatment of Mohajirs be entered into evidence.

propositions.text: RAD accepts the 2012 IRB document as it appeared in previous National Documentation Packages for Pakistan.
propositions.quote: The RAD will accept this document given that it is an IRB document which has appeared in previous versions of the National Documentation Package (NDP) for Pakistan.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants request a 2012 IRB document on Mohajirs; the court accepts it as it appeared in prior National Documentation Packages.

propositions.text: Rule 29 allows application to provide new documents with explanation of compliance with IRPA section 110(4) and relation to appellant.
propositions.quote: Rule 29 allows the Appellant to make an Application to provide a document not previously provided. Such an application must include an explanation of how the document meets the requirements of section 110(4) of the IRPA and how that evidence relates to the Appellant.

propositions.text: In deciding the application, RAD considers relevance, probative value, new evidence, and whether document could have been provided earlier with reasonable effort.
propositions.quote: In determining the Application, the RAD must consider any relevant factors, including the relevance and probative value of the document, any new evidence the document brings to the appeal, and whether the Appellant could have, with reasonable effort, provided the document with the Appellant's Record.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains Rule 29 allows new document applications with explanation and RAD considers relevance, probative value, newness, and reasonable effort.

propositions.text: Appellants request letters from principal appellant's wife, her sister, and twelve newspaper articles be entered as new evidence post-appeal submission.
propositions.quote: The Appellants ask that a letter from the principal Appellant's wife (the associate Appellant); a letter from her sister; and twelve newspaper articles be entered into evidence. In her affidavit, the associate Appellant stated that since the filing of the RAD appeal, the Appellants have researched and found new evidence regarding country conditions in Pakistan.

propositions.text: RAD accepts these items as they postdate appeal submission and are relevant to country conditions in Pakistan.
propositions.quote: The RAD will accept these items into evidence as they postdate the submission of the appeal and are relevant to country conditions in Pakistan.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants request letters and articles as new evidence post-appeal; the court accepts them as relevant and postdating appeal submission.

propositions.text: RAD may hold hearing if new evidence raises serious credibility issue central to decision and justifies allowing or rejecting claim.
propositions.quote: The RAD may hold a hearing if, in its opinion, there is documentary evidence referred to in section 110(3) that raises a serious issue with respect to the credibility of the person who is the subject of the appeal, is central to the decision with respect to the refugee protection claim, and, if accepted, would justify allowing or rejecting the refugee protection claim.

paragraphs.summary: The court states RAD may hold hearing if new evidence raises serious credibility issue central to decision and justifies claim outcome.

propositions.text: RAD can consider new evidence and assess probative value without oral hearing and chooses not to hold hearing under section 110(6).
propositions.quote: The RAD is able to consider the new evidence and assess its probative value without holding an oral hearing. Therefore, the RAD chooses not to hold a hearing under 110(6).

paragraphs.summary: The court decides to consider new evidence without oral hearing and declines to hold a hearing under section 110(6).

propositions.text: Appellants allege former counsel was incompetent and breached natural justice, filing a complaint with Law Society of Alberta.
propositions.quote: The Appellants have made several allegations regarding their former counsel's conduct and competence during their RPD process. They have provided a copy of the complaint they made to the Law Society of Alberta about their former counsel, XXXX XXXX.

propositions.text: Complaint contains fifteen points reflecting counsel's failures, including incomplete BOC, lack of legal advice, poor preparation, and failure to address ethnicity and children's fears.
propositions.quote: This complaint contains fifteen points relating to how the Appellants believe their counsel failed them. These points are reflected in the Memorandum of Appeal. The Appellants submit that there was a breach of natural justice due to the incompetence of Ms. XXXX. They submit the following: * Ms. XXXX did not diligently complete their BOC forms and failed to amend question 1(E) to reflect their ethnicity as Mohajirs; * Ms. XXXX did not advise them of the legal test they had to meet; * Ms. XXXX was not adequately prepared for their hearing as she failed to meet with them earlier than a few days before their hearing; failed to obtain a full account of the facts behind their claims; failed to question the principal Appellant regarding his ethnicity based fear; failed to make submissions regarding the Appellants' ethnicity; and failed to provide adequate research and independent evidence regarding the mistreatment of Mohajirs in Islamabad; * Ms. XXXX failed to prepare and question the principal Appellant regarding the fears of the minor children and did not make submissions accordingly; * Ms. XXXX failed to question the principal Appellant's son, wife and adult daughter (associate Appellants) about their fear of return; * Ms. XXXX conceded that there was no nexus to a Convention ground at the hearing without advising the Appellants; whereas the claim was based on imputed political opinion and membership in a social group; * Ms. XXXX failed to make meaningful submissions and did not refer to supporting personal documents; * Ms. XXXX failed to refer to the Chairperson's guidelines on Child refugee claimants; * Ms. XXXX told the Appellants that their hearing was perfect; and * Ms. XXXX told the Appellants after they asked why they had received a negative decision that she and the RPD member did not like each other.

paragraphs.summary: The appellants allege former counsel was incompetent, breached natural justice, and failed in many respects, filing a detailed complaint with the Law Society.

propositions.text: The RAD finds the Appellants did not follow required steps regarding allegations against former counsel Ms. XXXX per IRB practice notice.
propositions.quote: The RAD has considered the Immigration and Refugee Board (IRB) practice notice regarding allegations against former counsel and finds that the appropriate steps were not taken by the Appellants regarding their allegations against Ms. XXXX.

propositions.text: The IRB practice notice requires written allegations, notice to counsel, authorization release, and proof of delivery to counsel and Division.
propositions.quote: 5. Where the person alleges that they have been inadequately represented by their former counsel, the person must first provide former counsel with: a. a written statement containing the allegations...

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the Appellants did not follow IRB practice notice steps for allegations against former counsel Ms. XXXX, detailing required procedural steps.

propositions.text: No evidence shows Appellants complied with practice notice items 5, 6, or 8; former counsel was not notified or authorized to respond.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes that there is no evidence in the record that the Appellants complied with items 5, 6, or 8 of the practice notice.

propositions.text: Little weight can be given to allegations against former counsel without her opportunity to respond.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds therefore that little weight can be put on the allegations against the former counsel regarding her conduct and competence without her having had an opportunity to respond.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds no evidence Appellants complied with notice requirements and gives little weight to allegations against former counsel without her response.

propositions.text: The BOC narrative was detailed, signed by all adults, and adopted by all Appellants for RPD process.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes that the BOC narrative was eleven pages long and contained detailed information... All of the adult Appellants signed the BOC declaration... All of the Appellants adopted the BOC narrative...

propositions.text: It was reasonable for the RPD to question only the principal Appellant; no evidence others wished to testify.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds that it is reasonable in the circumstances that the RPD member chose only to question the principal Appellant.

propositions.text: Appellants submitted 340 pages of documentary evidence including personal documents and country conditions.
propositions.quote: The Appellants submitted 340 pages of documentary evidence for the hearing, which included personal documents, letters, and country condition documentation.

propositions.text: Given the detailed BOC and evidence, the hearing was reasonably not lengthy.
propositions.quote: Given the fulsomeness of the BOC narrative and the extensive supporting documentation, the RAD finds that it was reasonable that the hearing into these claims was not lengthy.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the BOC narrative detailed and adopted, questioning only principal Appellant reasonable, and hearing length reasonable given evidence.

propositions.text: RPD is expected to consider all relevant IRB guidelines and assess claims under sections 96 and 97 IRPA regardless of submissions.
propositions.quote: it is the expectation that all relevant guidelines are considered by the RPD member... it is also the expectation that the RPD will assess a claim under both sections 96 and 97 of the IRPA whether or not specific submissions have been made

propositions.text: The RPD assessed the claim under sections 96 and 97 and found no serious possibility of persecution or personal risk in Islamabad.
propositions.quote: the claim was ultimately assessed under both sections 96 and 97 as the RPD found that the Appellants would not face a serious possibility of persecution, or on a balance of probabilities a personal risk of harm in Islamabad.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD states RPD must consider guidelines and assess claims under IRPA sections 96 and 97; RPD found no serious risk in Islamabad.

propositions.text: IRB members must conduct themselves objectively per Code of Conduct; judicial impartiality presumes no bias without real likelihood.
propositions.quote: IRB members shall conduct themselves in a manner that will not cast doubt on their ability to perform their duties objectively... strong presumption of judicial impartiality... test for a reasonable apprehension of bias requires a "real likelihood or probability of bias".

propositions.text: No evidence of animosity or bias between former counsel Ms. XXXX and RPD member affecting conduct or decision.
propositions.quote: the RAD finds that it contains nothing to indicate that there was any animosity between the Appellants' former counsel Ms. XXXX and the RPD member... no evidence in the record that this in any way affected the member's conduct or even counsel's conduct during the hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds no evidence of animosity or bias between former counsel and RPD member; judicial impartiality presumes no bias without real likelihood.

propositions.text: Little weight is given to Appellants' allegations of incompetence against former counsel Ms. XXXX.
propositions.quote: the RAD finds that little weight can be given to the Appellants' allegations that their former counsel, Ms. XXXX, was incompetent when representing them during the RPD process.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD gives little weight to Appellants' allegations that former counsel was incompetent during RPD process.

propositions.text: RPD designated principal Appellant to represent two minor Appellants aged 16 and 11 at hearing.
propositions.quote: The RPD designated the principal Appellant to represent the two minor associate Appellants who were 16 and 11 years old at the time of the hearing.

propositions.text: RPD found family could relocate to Islamabad, a diverse city, living in relative peace and security.
propositions.quote: the RPD found that the family would be able to relocate to Islamabad and live in relative peace and security in that city which is considered an ethnically and religiously diverse location.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD designated principal Appellant to represent minors and found family could relocate safely to Islamabad.

propositions.text: Appellants argue RPD wrongly treated children as adults and failed to consider education, employment, vulnerability of Mohajir children.
propositions.quote: The Appellants argue that the RPD could not simply treat the children as if they were adults with the capacity to endure prejudice and discrimination.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants argue RPD wrongly treated children as adults and failed to consider their specific vulnerabilities.

propositions.text: Appellants argue RPD failed to recognize minor claimants' rights and threats to abduct and kill them.
propositions.quote: The Appellants argue that the RPD failed to recognize the minor claimant's rights and failed to recognize what can amount to persecution of a child.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants argue RPD failed to recognize minor claimants' rights and threats against them.

propositions.text: RAD reviewed Chairperson's Guideline 3 on child claimants; best interests and right to be heard must be considered.
propositions.quote: The RAD has reviewed the Chairperson's Guideline 3: Child and Refugee Claimants and Evidentiary Issues... the best interests of the child must be considered... a child has a right to be heard.

propositions.text: RPD stated at hearing no questions for other family members; counsel had no questions for them.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes that the RPD explicitly stated at the hearing that the panel did not have any questions for other members of the family and asked the Appellants' counsel whether she had any questions for the other Appellants to which she replied that she did not.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD notes child claimant guidelines and that RPD had no questions for other family members at hearing.

propositions.text: RAD finds RPD assessed documentary evidence and found all Appellants could relocate to Islamabad without risk from agents of persecution.
propositions.quote: The RAD finds that... the RPD had assessed the documentary evidence regarding the situation in Islamabad... and found that all of the Appellants could relocate to that city without a risk of harm from the agents of persecution.

propositions.text: RPD found it unlikely XXXX XXXX could find Appellants in Islamabad three years after last contact.
propositions.quote: The RPD found that it was unlikely that XXXX XXXX would have the willingness or ability to seek the Appellants across the country three years after they last had contact.

propositions.text: Principal Appellant testified about police harassment and kidnapping of his son but no other concerns about Islamabad relocation.
propositions.quote: the principal Appellant spoke about harassment from the police and stated that he could not risk taking his children there because he had already suffered the kidnapping of his son... he referred to police harassment and his fear that he would be implicated in a case for monetary reasons.

propositions.text: Principal Appellant did not testify about other problems if relocated to Islamabad despite being asked.
propositions.quote: he did not testify about any other problems he and members of his family would face should they relocate to Islamabad, despite being asked more than once about his concerns.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds RPD assessed evidence and found safe relocation to Islamabad; principal Appellant testified about police harassment and kidnapping only.

propositions.text: Principal Appellant made no allegations about children's ethnic treatment; RAD agrees RPD met IFA test for Islamabad.
propositions.quote: The RAD notes that the principal Appellant made no comments or allegations regarding treatment his children would receive because of their ethnic background... the RAD agrees with the RPD... that both prongs of the IFA test have been met in regard to Islamabad.

propositions.text: RPD conducted adequate assessment of IFA viability for whole family based on allegations and testimony.
propositions.quote: the RAD finds that the RPD conducted an adequate assessment of the viability of the IFA for the whole family based on the Appellants' allegations and the testimony provided by the principal Appellant.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds no ethnic treatment allegations and agrees RPD adequately assessed IFA viability for the family.

propositions.text: RPD found events prompting flight credible based on testimony and documents but found viable IFA in Islamabad.
propositions.quote: The RPD was satisfied that the events prompting the Appellants to flee Pakistan had taken place... the RPD found that the Appellants have a viable IFA in Islamabad.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the flight events credible but found a viable IFA in Islamabad.

propositions.text: Appellants argue RPD failed to establish nexus based on Mohajir ethnicity and ignored systematic discrimination.
propositions.quote: The Appellants argue that the RPD had established that the Appellants are Mohajirs at the hearing and yet failed to establish a nexus based on ethnicity.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants argue RPD failed to establish nexus based on Mohajir ethnicity and ignored discrimination.

propositions.text: Appellants submit RPD misconstrued evidence of mistreatment by XXXX XXXX related to ethnicity and discrimination.
propositions.quote: The Appellants submit that the RPD misconstrued evidence that the principal Appellant was mistreated by XXXX XXXX in Lahore which related to their ethnicity and the systematic discrimination and mistreatment of Mohajirs in Pakistan.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants submit RPD misconstrued evidence of ethnic mistreatment by XXXX XXXX.

propositions.text: Appellants argue RPD failed to analyze political opinion imputed by police accusing principal Appellant of terrorism and XXXX membership.
propositions.quote: The Appellants argue that the RPD failed to analyze all the elements of their claim which included the political opinion imputed on the principal Appellant by the police in Lahore who accused him of being a terrorist and a member of the XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants argue RPD failed to analyze political opinion imputed by police accusing principal Appellant of terrorism.

propositions.text: Appellants submit RPD ignored testimony that principal Appellant could only live in Karachi due to harassment and cultural distrust elsewhere.
propositions.quote: The Appellants submit that the RPD did not consider the principal Appellant's testimony that he could not live anywhere other than in Karachi because he had a bad experience with XXXX XXXX in Lahore...

paragraphs.summary: Appellants submit RPD ignored testimony that principal Appellant could only live in Karachi due to harassment and distrust.

propositions.text: Appellants argue RPD failed to analyze political opinion imputed by XXXX, mistreating Mohajirs opposed to XXXX.
propositions.quote: The Appellants argue that the RPD failed to analyse the political opinion imputed on them by the XXXX, as Mohajir opposed to the XXXX are severely mistreated by that party.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants argue RPD failed to analyze political opinion imputed by XXXX mistreating Mohajirs.

propositions.text: Appellants argue RPD failed to analyze risk from agents of persecution in Islamabad despite credibility and ties allowing tracking.
propositions.quote: The Appellants argue that the RPD failed to analyse the risk from the agents of persecution in Islamabad, given that the RPD found them to be credible and they had stated that the XXXX had sufficient ties with XXXX XXXX which would allow XXXX XXXX to find them in Islamabad.

propositions.text: Appellants submit RPD erred by ignoring evidence of severe competition and discrimination faced by Mohajirs from Punjabis.
propositions.quote: They submit that the RPD erred by not considering the documentary evidence which establishes that Mohajirs face severe competition from mainly Punjabis, who control government and military throughout Pakistan.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants argue RPD failed to analyze persecution risk in Islamabad and ignored evidence of Mohajir discrimination by Punjabis.

propositions.text: Appellants submit RPD had duty to consider sur place claim.
propositions.quote: The Appellants submit that the RPD had a duty to consider the sur place claim.

paragraphs.summary: Appellants submit RPD had duty to consider sur place claim.

propositions.text: Appellants did not argue fear of persecution based on Mohajir ethnicity at RPD hearing or in BOCs
propositions.quote: The RAD has reviewed the record and finds that the Appellants did not put forward an argument at the RPD hearing or in their BOCs that they fear of persecution in Pakistan based on their ethnic identity as Mohajirs.

propositions.text: Principal Appellant identified as Mohajir early at RPD hearing
propositions.quote: The RAD does note that the principal Appellant identified himself as a Mohajir early on at the RPD hearing.

propositions.text: Principal Appellant stated police in Lahore accused him of being a terrorist and Indian agent to extort bribes
propositions.quote: he stated that when he was living in Lahore he was approached by the police who asked to look at his documents which identified him as being from Karachi, and that he was told by the policeman that he must be an XXXX terrorist on the run. He stated that another time the police came to his home in Lahore and accused him of being an Indian agent. He stated that the police made these accusations both times in order to have him pay a bribe.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Appellants did not argue ethnic fear at RPD; principal Appellant identified as Mohajir and described police extortion attempts in Lahore.

propositions.text: RPD considered police extortion evidence and found Appellants speculated about police behavior in Islamabad
propositions.quote: The RPD addressed this information in its decision and found that the Appellants were speculating as to how the police in Islamabad would behave.

propositions.text: RPD distinguished Appellants' relocation from displaced persons fleeing conflict or disasters
propositions.quote: The RPD considered their submission that the documentary evidence states that police generally harassed displaced persons in Pakistan and found that the Appellants' putative relocation to Islamabad could be distinguished from the experience of internally displaced persons who relocate because of conditions such as armed conflict and natural disasters.

propositions.text: RPD found Appellants were affluent, educated urban people unlikely to face same vulnerabilities as displaced persons
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the Appellants were affluent, educated, urban people relocating for personal reasons and that it was unlikely that they would face the same disadvantages, vulnerabilities and police attention as compared to, for example, Pashtuns escaping from Khyber Pakthunkhawa.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD considered police extortion evidence, found Appellants speculated about Islamabad police, and distinguished their relocation from displaced persons.

propositions.text: Principal Appellant testified fearing gang in Islamabad, police harassment, language and cultural issues, and child kidnapping risk
propositions.quote: He testified that he feared that the gang would find him in Islamabad; that in the rest of the country police would harass them; that there is a language problem and a cultural difference; that the police and neighbours would consider him a suspicious person; and that he could not risk any of his children being kidnapped.

propositions.text: Principal Appellant stated police in Islamabad look at everyone suspiciously due to terrorism
propositions.quote: he stated that because there is so much terrorism in Islamabad the police look at every person suspiciously.

propositions.text: Principal Appellant did not testify to discrimination or persecution based solely on Mohajir ethnicity
propositions.quote: The principal Appellant did not testify to discrimination and persecution based solely on Mohajir ethnicity.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds principal Appellant feared gang, police harassment, cultural issues, and kidnapping risk in Islamabad but did not claim ethnic persecution.

propositions.text: RPD considered police corruption evidence and found insufficient evidence of systemic corruption
propositions.quote: RPD did consider the Appellants' concerns, and found that although there was evidence of police corruption, including demands for bribes, there was insufficient evidence to demonstrate that this corruption was systemic.

propositions.text: RPD found police corruption affected protection and arrest avoidance but no evidence police randomly demand bribes from unknown persons
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the documentary evidence suggested that obtaining effective state protection or avoiding arrest for those who would otherwise face arrest was affected by police corruption, but that there was insufficient evidence to suggest that the police randomly or systematically demand bribes from those who have not come to their attention.

propositions.text: Appellants only approached twice for bribes and had no other police problems
propositions.quote: The RPD noted that despite living in Pakistan for most of their lives, the Appellants were only approached for bribes by the police on two occasions and did not otherwise have problems in that regard.

propositions.text: RPD found no serious risk of persecution or harm in Islamabad and relocation was reasonable given personal circumstances and city's diversity
propositions.quote: The RPD found that the Appellants had not established that there was a serious risk of persecution or on a balance of probabilities a risk of harm in Islamabad, and that it was reasonable for the Appellants to relocate there considering their personal circumstances and that the city is an ethnically and religiously diverse location.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RPD found police corruption not systemic, Appellants had limited police contact, and relocation to diverse Islamabad was reasonable and safe.

propositions.text: RAD agrees with RPD that XXXX gang is local to Karachi and not established in Islamabad
propositions.quote: The RAD agrees with the RPD that the agent of persecution in Karachi, the XXXX XXXX gang, is local to that city.

propositions.text: Documentary evidence shows targeted killings and kidnappings in Karachi but insufficient evidence these crimes extend to other parts of Pakistan
propositions.quote: Although the documentary evidence provided by the Appellants does not indicate that this gang has a base of operations in Islamabad. Although the documentary evidence does state that there are targeted killings and kidnappings in urban Sindh, particularly Karachi, affecting both Mohajirs and Sindhis,11 there is insufficient evidence to suggest that those crimes against Mohajirs extend to other parts of the country.

propositions.text: Information request shows Mohajirs in Islamabad face severe competition and discrimination in government jobs only
propositions.quote: The RAD has considered the information request12 regarding the situation and treatment of Mohajirs in Islamabad and notes that the only concern documented was that they faced severe competition for and discrimination in government jobs.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RAD agrees gang is local to Karachi; crimes do not extend to Islamabad; Mohajirs face job discrimination only there.

propositions.text: Pakistan population approx. 200 million; Mohajirs about 7.5% or 14 million
propositions.quote: The RAD has considered that the population of Pakistan is approximately 200 million and that the Mohajir population constitutes 7.5%.

propositions.text: Insufficient evidence Mohajirs are systemically targeted for extortion or harm in Pakistan
propositions.quote: The RAD finds that there is insufficient evidence to indicate that this group of approximately 14 million people are systemically targeted for extortion or harm within Pakistan.

propositions.text: Appellants allege police target them for extortion once identity documents show Karachi origin
propositions.quote: Although the Appellants have alleged that once it is discovered from their identity documents that they are from Karachi, they will be targeted by the police for extortion,

propositions.text: RAD finds insufficient evidence that Karachi origin causes automatic targeting anywhere in Pakistan
propositions.quote: the RAD finds that there is insufficient evidence in the record or in the new documents provided by the Appellants that coming from Karachi would cause them to automatically be targeted anywhere in the country.

propositions.text: US Department of State Report states Karachi political parties and gangs vie for control and extortion privileges
propositions.quote: The RAD notes that the US Department of State Report13 states that in Karachi political parties and their affiliated gangs continue to vie for political and economic control and engage in a turf war over extortion collection privileges.

propositions.text: This gang conflict does not appear to extend beyond Karachi
propositions.quote: This however does not appear to extend to the rest of the country.

propositions.text: Report notes harassment and extortion of Afghani refugees by authorities and communities
propositions.quote: It is also noted in this document that there were reports of harassment and extortion of Afghani refugees by provincial authorities, police, and host communities.

propositions.text: Appellants do not fall into category of Afghani refugees
propositions.quote: As noted by the RPD, the Appellants would not fall into this category.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Pakistan has 200 million people; Mohajirs 7.5%; insufficient evidence of systemic targeting; Appellants allege police extortion but evidence does not support it.

propositions.text: Newspaper article about Peshawar policeman abducted in Islamabad is distinguishable from Appellants' situation
propositions.quote: The RAD finds that this situation can be distinguished from the Appellants' given that this individual was a member of the police force.

propositions.text: Appellants have no high profile government or police roles or political involvement
propositions.quote: The Appellants do not have high profiles as government or police employees and there is no indication on the record that they have ever had any political involvement.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the policeman abduction article is distinguishable; Appellants have no high profile or political roles.

propositions.text: Newspaper article states XXXX gang participated in 2018 elections and fielded candidates in Islamabad and other cities
propositions.quote: The RAD has also considered a newspaper article stating that the XXXX was taking part in upcoming elections in 2018 and that the XXXX would field candidates in Islamabad as well as other cities.

propositions.text: No indication gang or associates have established base in Islamabad
propositions.quote: However there is no indication in the article that the XXXX or associated gangs had established a base in that city.

propositions.text: Insufficient evidence gang has ties in Islamabad to find Appellant there
propositions.quote: The RAD finds that there is insufficient evidence in the record or in the new documents accepted into evidence on appeal that the XXXX or its associated criminal gang have ties in Islamabad that would allow them to find the Appellant in that city which is at the other end of the country from their base in Karachi.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds gang participated in 2018 elections but no base in Islamabad; insufficient evidence gang can find Appellant there.

propositions.text: Ethnic violence in Karachi involves turf wars between rival criminal groups backed by political parties
propositions.quote: there is evidence that in Karachi much of the ethnic violence in recent years has involved turf wars between rival criminal groups backed by political parties, such as the Awami National Party (ANP), a Pashtun nationalist party, and the MQM, which represents the interests of the Mohajir community.

propositions.text: No mention of such turf wars existing in Islamabad
propositions.quote: However, there is no mention that this sort of turf war exists in Islamabad.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds ethnic violence in Karachi involves political party-backed turf wars; no such turf wars exist in Islamabad.

propositions.text: Islamabad has about two million people including many internal migrants
propositions.quote: Islamabad has a population of around two million people, including a large number of internal migrants from all parts of the country.

propositions.text: Strong security presence with checkpoints and paramilitary Rangers patrols deters militant attacks
propositions.quote: There is a strong security presence, including checkpoints throughout the city and its entry points, and patrols by the paramilitary Rangers.

propositions.text: Large-scale militant or sectarian attacks in Islamabad are rare; violence usually targets high-profile community leaders
propositions.quote: large-scale militant or sectarian attacks in Islamabad are rare. Such violence more often takes the form of targeted killings (such as drive-by shootings) of high-profile community leaders.

propositions.text: Appellants are not community leaders or politically involved
propositions.quote: The Appellants have not identified as community leaders or being involved in any sort of politics.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Islamabad is populous with strong security; militant attacks are rare and target leaders; Appellants are not leaders or political.

propositions.text: Government uses military and paramilitary forces including Rangers and Frontier Constabulary for Islamabad security
propositions.quote: It is noted in the documentation that the government continued to use the military to support domestic security in Islamabad. Paramilitary forces, including Rangers and the Frontier Constabulary (FC), provided security to some areas of Islamabad

paragraphs.summary: The court finds government uses military and paramilitary forces to secure Islamabad.

propositions.text: Appellants can safely relocate to Islamabad without fear of gang or other targeting
propositions.quote: The RAD finds, as did the RPD, that the Appellants would be able to safely relocate to Islamabad without fear of being targeted by the gang from Karachi or any other source.

propositions.text: Given personal circumstances, relocation to Islamabad is reasonable; Appellants are educated and principal has business experience
propositions.quote: The RAD further finds that given their personal circumstances, relocating to Islamabad would be reasonable. As noted by the RPD they are educated and the principal Appellant has extensive business experience which would enable him to earn a living for the family.

propositions.text: No evidence Appellants unable to find housing or education if desired
propositions.quote: There is no evidence in the record that the Appellants would be unable to find appropriate housing or education should any of them wish to continue their education.

propositions.text: Insufficient evidence Appellants would face persecution-level discrimination in Islamabad; Mohajir difficulties in government jobs not relevant as Appellants do not seek government work
propositions.quote: The RAD finds that there is insufficient information in the record or in the new documents accepted with the appeal to indicate that the Appellants would experience discrimination in any form amounting to persecution in Islamabad. Although there is evidence that there are difficulties for Mohajirs in government employment, the Appellants have not alleged that they wish to work for the government or have had any experience in that regard.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Appellants can safely and reasonably relocate to Islamabad; no evidence of persecution or discrimination affecting them there.

propositions.text: Islamabad is a viable IFA for Appellants with no serious possibility of persecution or personal risk of harm
propositions.quote: The RAD finds, after considering all of the evidence, and given the Appellants' past and present circumstances, that Islamabad is a viable IFA for them and that there is not a serious possibility that they would suffer persecution in Islamabad or on a balance of probabilities a personal risk of harm in Islamabad.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Islamabad is a viable IFA with no serious risk of persecution or harm for Appellants.

propositions.text: Appellants argue RPD failed to consider IRB Gender Guidelines and gender-based persecution of female Appellants
propositions.quote: The Appellants provided an amended memorandum which additionally argued that the RPD failed to consider the IRB's Gender Guidelines. They argue that the RPD failed to analyse whether the female Appellants suffered persecution for reasons pertaining to kinship, and that there is new evidence of gender-based violence due to imputed political views and refusal to pay extortion demands by the principal Appellant.

propositions.text: Appellants did not specify which new evidence supports gender-based violence claim
propositions.quote: The Appellants, however have not specifically cited in their amended memorandum which new evidence they are referring to.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellants argue RPD failed to consider Gender Guidelines and gender-based persecution but did not specify new evidence.

propositions.text: Letter from principal Appellant's brother-in-law expresses fear for daughters but is speculative and unsupported by country documents
propositions.quote: he writes to his sister, the associate Appellant, "now that your daughters of grown-up, we fear that, God forbid, in your case you and your family come back and these people do something bad to your daughters or harm them, it will be the death of us." However, the RAD notes that this fear is not supported by any accompanying country condition documents and finds that this fear is speculative in regard to what could happen to the female Appellants.

propositions.text: Letter states XXXX XXXX seen with senator and visits Karachi, Islamabad, Punjab but lacks source and is not probative of gang presence in Islamabad
propositions.quote: Although it is written in the letter that XXXX XXXX is often seen with a senator belonging to XXXX and keeps visiting Karachi, Islamabad and the entire province of Punjab, this statement is not backed up by country condition documentation. The RAD finds that this letter is not probative in establishing that XXXX XXXX has established himself in Islamabad, given that the letter provides no indication as to the source of the information or how this information was acquired by the author of the letter.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the letter expressing fear for daughters is speculative and uncorroborated; gang presence in Islamabad not proven by letter.

propositions.text: New evidence is not probative of gender-based fear of persecution in Islamabad
propositions.quote: The RAD has considered its finding that Islamabad is a viable IFA for all of the Appellants and finds that the new evidence is not probative in establishing that there is a gender-based fear of persecution in that city based on new evidence provided by the Appellants.

propositions.text: Appellants did not identify gender-based fear in BOC or hearing
propositions.quote: The RAD further notes that the Appellants did not identify a gender-based fear of persecution in their BOC or at the hearing.

propositions.text: RPD did not err by not analyzing gender-based persecution for female Appellants
propositions.quote: The RAD finds that the RPD did not err by failing to analyse whether the female Appellants suffered persecution for reasons pertaining to kinship and gender-based violence.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds new evidence does not prove gender-based fear; Appellants did not claim it earlier; RPD did not err in analysis.

propositions.text: RAD conducted independent assessment of all evidence including new documents and Appellants' arguments
propositions.quote: The RAD has conducted an independent assessment of the all of the evidence contained in the RPD record as well as the new documents allowed with the appeal. The RAD has considered the Appellants' arguments contained in the memorandum and the amended memorandum.

propositions.text: Appellants did not establish denial of natural justice due to former counsel's conduct
propositions.quote: The RAD finds that the Appellants have not established they were denied natural justice because of their former counsel's conduct.

propositions.text: Islamabad is a viable IFA where Appellants can safely and reasonably reside
propositions.quote: The RAD finds that the Appellants have a viable IFA in Islamabad as they can safely and reasonably reside in that city.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds RAD independently assessed evidence, no denial of natural justice, and Islamabad is viable IFA for Appellants.

propositions.text: RAD dismisses appeal and confirms RPD decision that Appellants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection under IRPA section 111(1)(a)
propositions.quote: The RAD dismisses the appeal and confirms the decision of the RPD that the Appellants are neither Convention refugees nor persons in need of protection, pursuant to section 111(1)(a) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal and confirms RPD decision that Appellants are not refugees or in need of protection under IRPA.
